clue.text: Chance connection between wheels leads head of government to sign on — the like won't be seen again!

definitions.text: the like won't be seen again!

parts.note: hap is an old word for chance or luck
an axle joins a pair of wheels

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, so only the opening letter of government is used

parts.note: an omen is a sign of what is to come
taken as written

explanation.surface: A chance link between wheels leads a government chief to sign up for something unique.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leads' simply joins the pieces. A hapax legomenon is a word recorded only once in a language or text, hence nothing like it will be seen again.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek phrase names a word attested just once, a unique occurrence never repeated elsewhere.

clue.text: London location supplying English pork and cherry pie

indicators.note: printer's pie is jumbled type, so pie signals the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written, including the joining word

explanation.surface: A London spot serving an English pie of pork and cherries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pie' looks like the food but is the anagram signal: E with PORK AND CHERRY rearranges. HYDE PARK CORNER is a famous road junction and arch at the corner of Hyde Park in central London.
explanation.definitionFit: The junction beside Wellington Arch is a well-known named place in central London.

clue.text: Feverish City rep gets treatment

indicators.note: something given treatment is worked over and changed, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A feverish sales representative from the City receives medical care.
explanation.definitionFit: Pyretic is a medical adjective meaning relating to or suffering from fever.

clue.text: Drunken expat in public house has a nagging wife

indicators.note: drunken suggests staggering about, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written
PH is the map abbreviation for a public house

explanation.surface: A drunk expatriate in a pub has a wife who nags him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a container signal but is part of the fodder, rearranged by 'Drunken'. Xanthippe was the wife of Socrates, famed as a shrew.
explanation.definitionFit: Socrates' wife became proverbial as a shrewish, scolding spouse, so her name stands for any such woman.

clue.text: Girl stuffing sow with energy rays, by the sound of it

definitions.text: rays, by the sound of it

indicators.note: a filling stuffed into something sits inside it, so the girl goes within the pig

parts.note: an elt is a dialect word for a young sow
Eva is a girl's name
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A girl stuffs a pig with energy rays, it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a homophone: 'rays' sounds like 'raise', which is what the answer means. ELT, a young sow, is an old dialect word.
explanation.definitionFit: To elevate is to raise, and raise is said the same way as the clue's rays.

clue.text: Correspondence published in the "Gay Times"? It's the end of civilisation!

parts.note: a gay person who is open about it is said to be out
post is mail, letters received

explanation.surface: A readers' letters page in a gay magazine described as the death of civilised society.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters page of a gay magazine could be called its 'out post'. Gay Times is a real British magazine. 'published in the' and 'Times' dress the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: An outpost is a remote settlement at the frontier, where civilised territory ends.

clue.text: I brawl endlessly over plant extract

indicators.note: in a down clue over means turned upward, so the letters are read backwards
without its end, so the final letter of the word for brawl is dropped

parts.note: a melee is a confused brawl or scuffle

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to endless brawling over a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: MELEE loses its last E to give MELE; I + MELE turned over by 'over' gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Elemi is an aromatic resin obtained from tropical trees, used in varnishes and ointments.

clue.text: Not connected with unsavoury part of speech

parts.note: food that has gone off is bad, unpleasant
a line is a portion of a script that an actor speaks

explanation.surface: Something unrelated to a nasty grammatical category.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part of speech' suggests grammar (noun, verb), but here it is a line spoken in a play.
explanation.definitionFit: Being offline means disconnected from a network or the internet.

clue.text: Nightfall, at which is a cliché

definitions.meaning: the close of daylight hours, when evening comes
putting 'at' in front gives a tired stock phrase meaning 'ultimately'

explanation.walkthrough: Both senses rest on one phrase: literally the day's close, and, with 'at' prefixed, an overused filler expression.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally it means dusk; prefixed with 'at' it forms a notoriously worn-out spoken phrase.

clue.text: Drive mad queen into perilous situation, almost

indicators.note: one piece goes into the other, placing the queen inside
almost the whole word, so the last letter is cut off

parts.note: danger is a perilous situation
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the usual abbreviation for the Queen

explanation.surface: A queen pushed into peril is nearly driven insane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims the last letter, leaving DANGE, which 'into' opens to take the queen.
explanation.definitionFit: To derange is to make someone insane, to send them out of their mind.

clue.text: Glorious August day, or January night?

definitions.meaning: the Glorious ..., 12 August, opens the British grouse-shooting season
the night of 5 January, the last evening of Christmas, as in Shakespeare's play title

explanation.walkthrough: Both are well-known British dates: the start of grouse shooting in August, and the eve of Epiphany that ends Christmas festivities.
explanation.definitionFit: The ordinal names both 12 August, the grouse season's start, and the Epiphany eve of Shakespeare's comedy.

clue.text: Fling with frequency

definitions.meaning: the highness or lowness of a sound, governed by its rate of vibration

explanation.definitionFit: To pitch is to throw, and pitch is a tone's height set by its frequency of vibration.

clue.text: A tiresome character consuming single drink at the first local

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: eating something takes it inside, so the bore surrounds the other pieces

parts.note: a bore is a tedious person
I, the Roman numeral, is one
gin is a spirit

explanation.surface: A dull person knocking back a single gin at the local pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'local' looks like a pub, but the definition means the original inhabitant of a place.
explanation.definitionFit: An aborigine is one of the earliest known inhabitants of a land, its first natives.

clue.text: Addressee enlivened inert epic

indicators.note: brought to lively motion, so the letters are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone receiving a dull epic poem finds it brought to life.
explanation.definitionFit: The person a letter is addressed to is its recipient, the one who receives it.

clue.text: Compiler conceals name of old scold

indicators.note: to conceal is to hold hidden inside, so the setter's name surrounds a letter

parts.note: the compiler of this puzzle is the setter Shed

explanation.surface: The puzzle-maker hides the name of an old nag.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters sometimes refer to themselves: Shed set this puzzle. The definition is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Shend is an archaic verb meaning to rebuke or put to shame, a dated word for reproach.

clue.text: Unethical business exchange, involving hot food previously

indicators.note: to involve is to take in, so the exchange wraps around the other pieces

parts.note: swop is a variant spelling of swap

indicators.note: the food comes before, placing the food ahead of the hot

parts.note: eats is informal for food
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A shady firm swaps hot food in its dealings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'previously' puts the food before H, giving EATSH inside SWOP.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweatshop is a workplace exploiting labour with long hours and low pay, an unethical enterprise.

clue.text: Class's subject for investigation takes time

definitions.note: read as 'class is', the 's linking definition to wordplay

indicators.note: to take in something is to hold it within, putting the time inside

parts.note: a case is a matter investigated by police or a detective

explanation.surface: A class's research topic takes time.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'Class's' stands for 'is', so the definition is 'Class'.
explanation.definitionFit: A caste is a hereditary social class, especially in the Hindu system.

clue.text: Require commitment from the strings, perhaps

definitions.meaning: to compel someone's detention in a psychiatric hospital under mental health law
one division of an orchestra, such as violins and cellos

explanation.walkthrough: In Britain, to section someone is to detain them under the Mental Health Act.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means detaining a patient compulsorily, and the noun names an orchestral group such as strings.

clue.text: When to take in conviction for artwork

indicators.note: the pieces are put in the larger word

parts.note: a firm belief is a conviction
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
R stands for recipe, Latin for take, used on prescriptions

explanation.surface: When convicted, someone gets taken in for their art.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conviction' suggests a criminal sentence but means a firmly held belief. R for recipe ('take') is an old prescription convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Bas-relief is sculpture whose figures project slightly from a flat background, a form of artwork.

clue.text: Scope for life to absorb origin of death

indicators.note: to absorb is to take in, so the first letter goes inside the word for life

parts.note: breath is the sign of life

indicators.note: the origin of a word is its start, so only the first letter of death

explanation.surface: There is room for life to take in the beginnings of death.
explanation.definitionFit: Breadth means range or extent, as with the scope of a study.

clue.text: Leave shore when the scenery's looking the worse for wear?

parts.note: theatre scenery is made up of sets
to ail is to be in poor health, run-down

explanation.surface: Departing from land just when the stage scenery looks shabby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scenery's looking the worse for wear' reads cryptically as 'sets ail'.
explanation.definitionFit: To set sail is to begin a voyage, departing from land.

clue.text: In modern parlance, I emphatically eschew having regular teeth

parts.note: taken as written
so is used as an emphatic intensifier in modern speech
to eschew something is to avoid it, i.e. to not do it, as in 'I don't'

explanation.surface: A modern speaker insists they shun neat teeth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In modern parlance' signals the trendy 'I so don't' construction. Isodont describes animals whose teeth are all alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Isodont is a zoological term for having all teeth of equal size and shape, uniform dentition.

clue.text: City, seized by strange inclination, goes belly up

indicators.note: seized by means held within, so the city goes inside

parts.note: rum is British slang for odd or strange
EC is the postcode for the City of London
a bent is a natural inclination or talent

explanation.surface: A city in the grip of odd desires goes bankrupt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'belly up' suggests business failure, but here it means lying on one's back. 'goes' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Recumbent means lying down, reclining, as one lying face upward would be.

clue.text: Animal's low points

definitions.note: read as 'animal is', the 's linking definition to wordplay

parts.note: to low is to moo, as cattle do
S and E are compass points

explanation.surface: An animal's worst moments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'low' is the cattle noise, not a depth; 'points' gives two compass points.
explanation.definitionFit: The moose is a large deer of northern forests, an example of an animal.

clue.text: Antiquated trust is to run hospital

parts.note: to trot is to run at a gentle pace

explanation.surface: Old-fashioned faith in jogging to the hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: Troth is an archaic word for faithfulness or a pledged word, as in plighting one's troth.

clue.text: Lingy little Spaniard interrupting religious festival

indicators.note: breaking into something means getting inside it

parts.note: Eid is a Muslim festival
Rico is a pet form of the Spanish name Ricardo

explanation.surface: A small Spaniard breaks into a religious celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: Ling is heather, so 'Lingy' means heather-like.
explanation.definitionFit: Ericoid means resembling heath plants, and ling is the common heather.

clue.text: Kentish town is, like, in favour of obstructing Lawrence's return

parts.note: as means like

indicators.note: something obstructing a path sits in its way, so a word goes inside
a return goes back, so the initials are read backwards

parts.note: D. H. Lawrence the novelist is known by his initials
for means supporting

explanation.surface: A Kent town is, like, keen to block Lawrence's comeback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' turns the novelist's initials round to HD. Ashford is a town in the English county of Kent.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashford is a market town in Kent, south-east England.

clue.text: Point to mushroom ring for saint on the way into state of brain damage

parts.note: E, east, is a compass point

indicators.note: the pieces go into the state abbreviation

parts.note: NY is New York

indicators.note: put on means placed next, so the way follows the ring

parts.note: a cep is an edible mushroom
a halo is the ring shown around a saint's head
a path is a way

explanation.surface: A mushroom ring placed on a saint's path points to brain damage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'state of' reads as part of the definition, but the state is NY, housing CEP, HALO and PATH.
explanation.definitionFit: Encephalopathy is a medical term for disease or damage affecting the brain.
